summary: Searched N[T] identities 4/P(T)=1/X1+1/X2+1/X3 with deg P<=2, P(1)=n in {5,13,17}, deg X1,X2<=2 with coeffs<=6 (X3 solved exactly, all verified as polynomial identities): 7, 5, 1 P's admit one (n=5,13,17). Every family is classical: 2+3T gives 4/(3t+2)=1/(t+1)+1/(3t+2)+1/((t+1)(3t+2)) (all n≡2 mod 3); 5+8T gives x=(3n+1)/8,y=(3n+1)/4,z=n(3n+1)/4 (all n≡5 mod 8); 5+6T+6T^2 lies in n≡2 mod 3. Residues of P(t) mod 840 hit Mordell's six classes {1,121,169,289,361,529} only via composite values t(3t+2) (P=2T+3T^2), whose ES follows from the classical n≡2 mod 3 family by divisor closure; no prime value in those classes.
not_done: Higher degree P and X_i (only deg<=2 X1,X2, coeffs<=6; X3 unrestricted in degree); no search for identities at other n.
next: Search deg-3 P in N[T] for n in the Mordell classes {1,121,169,...} mod 840 and check whether any identity family yields prime values there.

summary: Enumerated all ES solutions for n<=20000 (C, scripts/z52d_p2_NC0_Z0524.c) and tested for each q in 2..12 and r mod q whether some 4/n=1/x+1/y+1/z has x≡y≡z≡r (mod q). Local rule (PROVED): for gcd(n,q)=gcd(r,q)=1, 3n≡4r (mod q) is necessary; so for odd n, (q,r)=(8,odd) and (4,1),(4,3),(10,odd) etc. have no admissible coprime n. In the non-vacuous admissible classes failures remain: (5,1) 38 of 4000 (all 38 prime), (5,2) 83 of 3999 (81 prime), (7,3) 78 of 2857 (74 prime), (11,7) 181 of 1819 (72 prime). No non-vacuous (q,r) is failure-free.
not_done: n beyond 20000 (about 5 min per 2e4 on one core, cost rising superlinearly); 'coprime to 6' and 'n with gcd(n,q)>1' not tabulated separately; no test of whether the composite failures are exceptions to primality.
next: Re-run the admissible-class failure count for (5,1) and (5,2) at n<=2e5 to see whether the failures are exactly the Mordell-hard primes.

summary: Premise check: the 'threshold' needs the largest prime not covered by parameter-≤K identities; but Mordell's covering identities leave exactly the six classes {1,121,169,289,361,529} mod 840 uncovered (the classes are ≡1 mod 24, so they are never covered by any parameterised identity family, and K does not enter). Counting: 2370 primes ≤10^6 lie in these six classes (smallest 1009, 1129, 1201, 1801, 2521; largest 999961), so for every K the set of primes not covered by parameter ≤K is infinite and no finite escalation threshold exists for the known identity list. Z0264's N[T] search reproduces only classical families (no new class).
not_done: Did not construct the explicit parameterised identity list per class (the classes outside M6 are covered by identities indexed by t; the K-dependence only moves the covered range, not the uncovered classes). Did not test a 'finite escalation' for variant U (its failure list is a different object, see Z0609).
next: Replace the K-threshold by a closure test: for each K, list the primes p ≤ 10^6 in M6 that a K-bounded search certifies (none expected), to make the 'no threshold' statement numerical.

summary: Premise check: the 'sporadic U(n)' list {105, 2961, 3985, 25305, 111969, 978145} belongs to CONJECTURE U (s5_unforced_words.md, a different word-count), not to the ES solution count: the ES count (scripts/z52b_p1_U05_ucount.c, = A192787 definition) gives 264, 2221, 206, 7733, 57208, 4680 at these n, and is positive for all 2≤n≤3000. Proved fact: d|n ⇒ count(n) ≥ count(d) (scaling injection), checked on 21496 divisor pairs with 0 violations, so the ES exceptional set is divisor-closed in the failing direction and has no composite structure to find below 3000.
not_done: Did not analyse the CONJECTURE U object (word/Jacobi-genus structure) since it is not the item's question; did not extend ES count beyond the values listed.
next: Relabel the fingerprint claim 'U(n)=A192787' vs 'U(105)=0' conflict in BRAINSTORM so that the two U's are distinguished.

summary: Ran the F_q[T] ES engine (A=T, 3 monic denominators) over all monic irreducible P with T∤P: q=5 deg≤6 (failures 2,2,1,0,0), q=7 deg≤5 (failures 6,21,25,16 of 21,112,588,3360). At q=7, n=4,5 the failure rate rises monotonically with the number of irreducible factors of P−1 (n=5: 0/560 at 1 factor, 2/1162, 6/1057, 5/448, 3/133 at 5 factors; mean #factors 3.56 failing vs 2.53 ok). The 'P−1 has an F_5-root' pattern found at q=5 fails at q=7 (9 of 68 failing P have no root), and there is no degree-matched control yet.
not_done: No degree-profile-matched control (the trend may be a generic #factors effect); q=7 and q=5 at n=6 for q=7 (≈10^4 P) not run; the EXSET_FUNCTION_FIELD exception list was not used (engine decides directly).
next: Port es_solutions to C and run q=7 and q=11 at n=6 with a profile-matched control on P−1 factor degrees.

summary: Over F_3 with A=T, every monic irreducible P (T∤P) of degree 2..7 (3+8+18+48+116+312 primes) has a solution T/P=1/X+1/Y+1/Z with X,Y,Z monic and pairwise distinct; each solution is checked by exact polynomial identity (assert), and the completeness of the search rests on the degree-(n−1) lemma of bs_ff_es, validated against brute force for n≤3 (0 missing solutions). So the distinct-denominator variant shows no failure up to deg 7 (Z0047 step done, empty).
not_done: Degree 8 (810 primes, est. ~40 min more on one core) not run; the engine's char≥5 restriction was bypassed for Q=3 (validated by brute force at n≤3 only); no 4/P-type numerator tested (A=T as in the FF engine).
next: Run degree 8 over F_3 (≈40 min) in C if the deg≤8 bound of the item is required.

summary: Over F_5 (A=T), the 3-term engine fails on 5 irreducible P (deg 2: 2, deg 3: 2, deg 4: 1) and succeeds for all deg 5,6 (2580). A 4-term search with X1,X2 of degree ≤ n−1 (sufficient, not complete) finds nothing, but widening to degree ≤3 (n=2,3) and ≤4 (n=4) gives exact 4-term witnesses for all 5 (identity checked by assert), e.g. T/(T²+2) = 1/T + 3/(T(T²+2)) (repeated denominators, using 5=0); for P=T⁴+T²+2T+2 the witness has denominators of degrees 3, 4, 7 and 13. So the 3-term failures are removed by 4 terms at this size, with largest witness denominator degree ≈ 3n for n=4.
not_done: Only deg ≤4 for the 3-term failures (deg 5,6 have none); 4-term witnesses not required to be distinct (the Z0047 distinctness variant not checked for 4 terms); no q=7 run; no completeness claim for the 4-term search (witness-only).
next: Check whether the 5 witnesses can be chosen with pairwise-distinct denominators (apply the Z0047 distinctness filter to the 4-term search at deg ≤ n+1).
